data.narrative:
Silicon Box is a Series B chip design company founded by Han Byung Joon, Sehat Sutardja, and Weili Dai, having raised $200M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 private peers and 3 public semiconductor companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD), with relevant private peers including Positron AI, Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and others at similar or adjacent funding stages.

Two quantitative methods are applicable. Stage-Progression applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $200M total raised as a valuation proxy, implying $380M. Peer-Median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.5B, with a range spanning $529M (DEEPX, Series C) to $11.0B (SambaNova, Series A). Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples is not applicable given the absence of disclosed target revenue data. Triangulating the two applicable methods produces a range of $323M to $1.7B, with a median of $940M.

The wide dispersion between stage-progression and peer-median results—spanning nearly 4.5x—reflects material heterogeneity in frontier semiconductor valuations and stage dynamics. The peer set itself exhibits pronounced variance ($529M to $11.0B), indicating that stage, technical differentiation, and capital efficiency drive valuations more than sector membership alone. Key uncertainties include Silicon Box's revenue trajectory, R&D efficiency relative to peers, and addressable market definition within chip design.
